review_text: Believe the hype, this game is the best thing sliced bread! Don't let the movement mechanics scare you, Respawn did amazing with the controls and feeling of the whole game - ♥♥♥♥♥ buttery smooth, can't get good stuff like this anywhere else! The single-player AND multiplayer of this game is absolutely the GOAT, hands down. Anyone who says its not simply hasn't played it, and here's a little secret for multiplayer - the games still fun even when you lose, you're saddened by the fact that the match is over - winning or losing is an afterthought. Between the Titans and movement mechanics, the perfect story mode, you'll be surprised that "it all just works" and realize this game is lightning in a bottle. No exaggeration, add about 1,600+ hours to time played at time of review - I got this on Xbox when it came out so I'm guessing based off time I spent on games here on Steam. Could probably double that if the DDOS attack on the servers bullspit hadn't gone on for a couple years...

God I could write a novel on my mixed feelings on this one - approaching 6 years of 2077 here, good lorde. Few games had me as hyped as Cyberpunk 2077. From its 2015 reveal to the delayed 2020 launch, I was completely locked in, in 2015 I basically discovered the cyberpunk genre through the world Mike Pondsmith created. It felt like the perfect middle ground between overdone fantasy and surface-level sci-fi. This was the only game I have ever preordered. I played it at launch on PC and, despite bugs like T-posing, broken AI, and weird visual glitches, I still enjoyed my first run. A lot of the bigger issues felt fixable, and I was more excited for what the game could become. Things like deeper RPG systems, meaningful AI, gang dynamics, and customization all felt like they were coming later. That is where the disappointment really sets in. Even now in 2026, after patches and Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty, it never became the RPG it was presented as. If you were (like me) expecting something closer to The Witcher but in a cyberpunk setting, this is not that. And yet I have played through it six+ times. Because what is here is still incredible. Night City is one of the most detailed and immersive worlds ever made. Just driving around, watching the skyline, and existing in that space is unmatched. It honestly feels like the scale and ambition of the world came at the cost of the systems meant to support it. Amazing world, unforgettable vibe, but a missed RPG opportunity, and they clearly knew it from how they focused on all its positives in Phantom Liberty.

Stardew Valley. It was a game I turned to when I lost the passion I once held for my college degree. The game that returned me to my roots, to a time when I was a child playing Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town on my GameBoy Advance. A time when farming was a way for me to feel productive, when the term "job" was yet foreign to me. And now, as an adult 20 years later, I get to enjoy that time with a game that continues to provide for the community, with new updates, new farms, new pets, and so much more than I could have imagined on my own. And my 800+ hours will only grow further as the next 20 years pass. Thank you, ConcernedApe, for bringing back such wonderful memories and helping me relive them every time I play.

Never goes super in depth with its mechanics or balances them well. Not even the start feels that balanced. But it does enough with what it has to keep you playing. It definitely does tickle your bone in your body that likes to explore from time to time (lest you'll probably have to wiki-dive for questions you have). The highlight of the game isn't really the farming. Everything related to crops or animals isn't that rewarding besides easy money. There's maybe a few days of unique content that you'll likely care about, everything else is intermittent. The other skills will probably interest you more if you want more active gameplay. Many say to not do a modded playthrough the first time but I would say honestly give it a shot if the game doesn't interest you in some aspects. I've had way much more fun with faster animations + marriage mod (the marriage candidate pool is limited and the gameplay loop is a bit slow, especially when trying to go through all its content). I probably would've had even more fun with something like SDVE (Stardew Valley Expanded) as it mostly adds on to already existing content. This is a really safe pick if you want to play something low-pressure with your friends so it's also great for that.

rating this on the singleplayer campaign because: 1) thats all ive played thus far, and 2) that's what's most likely to stick around in the future. it was a short campaign, but really good. i knew nothing going in other than "this game has freerunning, its older (game is from 2016, played in jan2026), you can control mechs, and people seem to play it for multiplayer a lot". it shows its age a bit in several minor ways, but even in 2026, im pretty happy with what i played. the gameplay isnt without its minor qualms, but nothing annoying. mouse was snappy with no acceleration or damping, controls were all responsive, fov was more than enough, game is very efficient on cpu and gpu even with multiple browsers full of tabs in the background. go in blind, maybe play the first game first, for story. I didnt think i'd care about the story at all in this, but coming out, it's what i cared about most. it took me maybe 10-15 hours of non-rushing and sorta screwing around here and there. gunplay is... acceptable. its not bad by any means, but ammo scarcity and encouraging you to play scrappily and swap weapons because there's no ammo of what you've been using, and not remembering ammo or even guns between missions is ass, but wasnt impactful at all. just kind of a minor annoyance in this game. if i had to put a value on this game, specifically for just the singleplayer campaign, i'd say it's worth.... honestly, 10-20 usd, maybe more, depending on your expectations. it WAS very short, but i rarely finish games these days because im so picky, and i actually finished this in two casual evening sessions. not sure if i'd play multiplayer of this. i'll give it a try, but i have some ideas how it'll go.... so yeah: value: 10-20 usd visuals: A, older but very creative sound: A-, very good, some very small wishes gameplay: A, actually fun story: A+, almost cried overall: solid A AGAIN: GO IN BLIND, DONT EVEN WATCH THE TRAILER edit: i just read about the history of tf1, apex, and ea... and dude? ♥♥♥♥ ea SO much. this is, once again, ea just destroying anything they touch. damnit. im upset that this is what's happened, and now im upset that im in on the knowledge that this is what's happened. titanfall fans: i see you, now. you are valid.
